symptom: ako/mxcli#2121: a REPL session never saw a write by another process (a second mxcli exec, Studio Pro, git): `show microflows` kept the old set, `describe microflow` of a flow created elsewhere said `microflow not found`, and on MPR v2 the session's own `create microflow` of that name wrote a SECOND document with it; on v1 (#2115 already re-read the listing) `create entity` in a module made elsewhere still said `module not found`.
cause: Two layers cached with no external-change signal: the v2 reader's unit index (unitCacheValid, cleared only by this reader's own writes) and the executor's executorCache (modules, domain models, hierarchy, name maps), which nothing but a session write ever reset. A git checkout also replaces the .mpr by rename, which an open SQLite connection never sees: it goes on reading the old inode.
file: modelsdk/mpr/reader_disk_change.go (SyncWithDisk: PRAGMA data_version + os.SameFile on the .mpr), mdl/backend/modelsdk/backend.go (SyncWithDisk reopens on replacement, refuses while a deferred run holds writes), mdl/executor/disk_change.go (called at the top of Execute; dropProjectReads keeps created/dropped/modifiedDomainModels)
insight: Probe, don't re-read: PRAGMA data_version moves only for OTHER connections' commits (the reader holds one connection), so the session's own writes never trip it and #2094's caches survive; file size/mtime would fire on every own write and undo that perf work. data_version cannot see a file renamed into place, so add os.SameFile on the path. The v1 symptom survived #2115 because the stale cache was the executor's, not the reader's — test with two executors (two backends = two SQLite connections) on a copy of both the v1 and the v2 fixture, and assert at the executor, not the reader. Stubbing only the executor-cache drop leaves `module not found` failing on both formats, which is the control that shows both layers are needed. The write-from-stale-state case was a duplicate document (v2 create of a name taken elsewhere), not a lost update: domain-model writes re-read the unit and kept the other process's entity in every measured run. Not covered: a change between one statement's read and its write (the locking proposal), and a v2 change to mprcontents/ with the .mpr untouched.
